subject: Re: Implementable training ban — technical constraints and DPA amendment
messages:

Subject: Initial ask — training prohibition + proofflow

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As we discussed with procurement, HealthBridge needs an explicit, contractually binding prohibition on using our customer data to improve models (training, fine-tuning, or parameter updates).

We also need a lightweight operational proofflow: what artifacts will Redwood provide to demonstrate our data was not used for model training (for audits and internal compliance). Ideally this includes:
- a DPA amendment or clause we can sign that states no-training/no-derivatives for our tenant data;
- an attestation procedure or one-click evidence export (logs, retention policy, subprocessor list); and
- confirmation of how cross-border routing and caching are handled (we cannot have data routed outside of US/US-controlled regions for training-related pipelines).

Can you confirm whether the no-training commitment is implementable without breaking latency/throughput SLAs for our interactive use? If there are technical caveats (e.g., reduced caching or costly route pinning), please call them out so procurement can evaluate tradeoffs.

We can share a DPA redline on our side — I attached the current legal team's starting point. Looking for a straightforward plan and timeline.

Best,
Ellen Hayes
Head of Privacy, HealthBridge

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. We're aligned on the ask and have sketched an operational approach. High level: yes, we can offer a contract-level prohibition on using HealthBridge data for model improvement, but there are implementation tradeoffs we'll need to document so procurement can evaluate.

Summary of what we'll deliver if we include a no-training clause: 
- Contract amendment (we'll propose language) stating Redwood will not use tenant data to train or tune models, and will not derive model checkpoints from customer inputs.
- Evidence pack on request (audit package): requestable export that includes request-level routing logs, subprocessor access logs (last 90 days), and a signed attestation from our security team. Note: this is an on-demand export, not continuous streaming.
- Operational constraints and recommended options:
  * Option A (isolation+no-cache): pin tenant to isolated serving pool + disable prefix/KV caching for that tenant — strongest technical guarantee; incurs higher per-token cost and potential throughput impact.
  * Option B (logical no-training + ephemeral KV): maintain shared pools but ensure data is processed in-memory without retention to training queues; KV caching allowed but with eviction and strict non-persist policy — lower cost but weaker forensic guarantees.

I've looped in Dev (dev_patel) for the technical breakdown and Marissa (sales) to coordinate commercial impact. We'll send a redline to your DPA and a short tech note describing metrics and SLO impact.

Next steps: Dev to provide estimated latency and cost delta for Option A vs Option B. Marissa will scope contractual language and revenue/discount implications. I'll prepare the attestation template.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jasmine Liu

Ellen, Jasmine — technical notes below (high level + measurable impacts). I kept it concise so procurement has what it needs to decide.

Baseline: HealthBridge uses our interactive/chat endpoints with 95p latency target ~180ms at steady state. Shared GPU pools use persistent KV caches and prefix caching to reduce token compute and keep costs low.

Option A — Isolation + Full No-Retention (strongest):
- Implementation: dedicate a tenant-only serving pool (single-tenant containers), disable prefix/KV cache persistence, strip request telemetry from any async training pipelines.
- Guarantees: Forensic posture strong — logs show no writes to training stores; no shared cache artifacts.
- Impact: +20–40% per-token cost; peak throughput reduction ~15% per-GPU depending on concurrency; provisioning lead time 2–3 weeks for reserved capacity provisioning.

Option B — Shared Pool + Runtime Non-Persist (operationally cheaper):
- Implementation: shared serving with runtime flags that avoid writing customer data to persistent training queues, strict 0-disk persistence policy, and truncated ephemeral KV lifetimes.
- Guarantees: Operational but requires internal controls and attestation; potential edge cases where debug captures (rare) could include snippets unless we disable debug capture for the tenant.
- Impact: +5–10% per-token cost; minimal throughput change; near-term rollout (1 week) to flip flags.

Evidence / Proofflow we can provide:
- Routing logs (request id, serving pool, region) — CSV export.
- Subprocessor access report — who viewed logs or had access (last 90 days).
- Attestation PDF signed by Head of Security and Head of Product stating no-training compliance for the specified date range.

Operational caveats:
- If HealthBridge requests regional pinning to a single AWS region for both serving and storage, that is feasible but increases operational cost and will require a committed monthly minimum for Dedicated or Private deployment.
- For high-volume interactive use, Option A may require reserved capacity to hit latency SLOs.

If this looks right, I can produce a short matrix with numeric cost deltas (usd/token) and expected provisioning times.

— Dev Patel
SVP, Serving & Runtime
Redwood Inference
